generation: The baseline is the cooking method and portion reference. Preserve its flavor-building order and quantities of unchanged fresh ingredients.
Scale quantities to requested servings ONCE. Added ingredients must not cause multiplying all remaining seasonings or broth.
Keep instructions brief, one essential action per bullet, and prepare cutting before cooking.

Available ingredients are candidates: choose only those suitable for one coherent dish. Every ingredient in the output must be used in a cooking phase, but not every available candidate must be included. Preserve the requested dish identity and its defining ingredients. Do not add unavailable seasonings. Do not enumerate unused candidates.
Announce heat before heating. Frying and simmering require an explicit heat and timer.
Do not substitute boiling for baseline frying aromatics, kimchi or meat. Preserve cold-oil chili blooming when the baseline specifies it.
If a missing ingredient makes the source technique impossible, disclose the limitation instead of claiming the same flavor.

Instructions must be short essential cooking actions. Omit equipment-type disclaimers, manufacturer guidance, setup/stability checks and redundant process explanations. For pan frying, give oil-first preheating as a direct action without adding oil twice. Preserve actual doneness cues and technique-critical heat order.
